sampling_model.design: Four-block strong-factor panel experiment with one unobserved counterfactual mean and a donor-only spectral construction.
sampling_model.units: For each \(n\), the donor block is \(n\times n\), the target row is \(1\times n\), and the target column is \(n\times1\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment masks the lower-right untreated potential-outcome entry; identification of its mean follows from the exact rank and span restrictions.
sampling_model.overlap: No target-loading lower bound is imposed; donor singular values satisfy \(cn\le s_r(A)\le s_1(A)\le C_0n\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Known \(r\) and \(\sigma\); \(A\), its singular spaces, and both target loading coordinates are unknown and estimated only through the real Gaussian observations \(X,R,C\). The certified implementation first applies the measurable map \(\mathsf{Enc}_{p_n,L_n}\) and retains an explicit encoding-exception flag.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives Gaussian entrywise inference under condition \(4.4\mathrm{c}\).  The present upper guarantee removes that condition only on the canonical square one-target subclass proved by the embedding proposition; the local lower bound on this subclass transfers to any containing class because honesty on the larger class implies honesty on the subclass.
Theorems 4.1--4.2 give uniformly valid minimum-distance inference for first-order-degenerate smooth transformations from a uniformly Gaussian primitive estimator.
Appendix C proposes a first-order bilinear interval and states that analogous validity requires modified projected-loading conditions.
Residuals from computed SVD factors produce verified enclosures for singular values.
Truncated SVD has explicit first- and second-order perturbation expansions and normwise remainder bounds.

body.tldr: A strong donor block identifies a missing untreated panel mean as \(\theta_n=uA^+v\), but the usual Gaussian interval loses uniform validity when both target loading projections approach zero. The donor-only interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) retains the independent bilinear donor-noise term through an exact conditional Gaussian reduction, covers uniformly over fixed-rank strong-factor panels, has expected length of order \(w_n=a_n+b_n\), recovers the Gaussian oracle constant along every first-order-dominant sequence, and meets a local Kullback--Leibler length lower bound. The computational layer separates a deterministic directed-arithmetic theorem for bounded exact dyadic arrays from a measurable rounding map applied to the real Gaussian observations; the open transfer asks for polynomial bit complexity and encoding-plus-arithmetic padding that is uniformly negligible, including \(o(n^{-1})\) padding at rank-one joint zero.

project_justification.gap: Existing four-block panel intervals are sharp only after a target-loading lower bound, while generic first-order-degeneracy inference assumes that the primitive Gaussian experiment and its covariance are already available. Neither literature controls donor-SVD target drift at the quadratic \(n^{-1}\) width or certifies floating-point endpoints.
project_justification.niche: Known-rank Gaussian strong-donor panels isolate a finite-dimensional bilinear reduced experiment while retaining the repeated-spectrum, joint-zero, and arbitrarily slow-transition cases that defeat a single delta-method normalization.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the donor-conditional experiment, constructs an analytic outer interval with an observable donor allowance and bounded fallback, proves transition-order upper and lower length results, and separates the unresolved implementation into a deterministic exact-dyadic enclosure theorem and a measurable encoding transfer under the continuous Gaussian experiment.

body.related_work: Yan and Wainwright (2024) supply the identical four-block spectral estimator, regular Gaussian interval, and genie-aided lower-bound architecture; the present strict comparison is removal of their loading-sensitive interval condition while controlling length at the surviving bilinear scale. Bei and Navjeevan (2026) motivate minimum-distance inversion near a zero gradient and are used as an inference exemplar, not as a theorem-level target, because their results start from a uniformly Gaussian primitive estimator. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016) motivate nuisance-robust inversion under weak identification. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright (2025) make entrywise and bilinear counterfactual intervals operational for staggered adoption, but their Appendix C remains a first-order sketch with projected-loading conditions. Bordino, Berrett, and Klopp (2026) directly estimate multilayer bilinear forms and establish mean-squared-error bounds, but do not supply a confidence-interval or loading-degeneracy theorem. Bai and Ng (2021) establish the strong-factor tall-wide counterfactual tradition. Terao, Watanabe, and Ozaki (2025), Dopico and Moro (2004), and Vu, Chunikhina, and Raich (2021) inform the deterministic exact-dyadic SVD certificate but do not transfer it through a measurable encoding of continuous statistical observations. IEEE 754-2019 fixes directed-rounding semantics; the target additionally requires explicit rescaling, exceptional-state certificates, and outward special-function evaluation. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025) provide a broader synthetic-control uncertainty benchmark without the strong-factor transition-length frontier.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact-real statistical interval and its analytic outer formula remain claims to prove. The unresolved numerical layer has two distinct obligations: a worst-case theorem for bounded exact dyadic arrays under directed arithmetic, and a statistical transfer after measurable rounding of the continuous Gaussian blocks. The latter must propagate coordinate encoding error, clipping probability, outward SVD and pseudoinverse errors, directed normal and chi-square quantiles, exponent growth, and spectral-gate uncertainty in both probability and expectation. Rank-one joint-zero loadings leave width of order \(n^{-1}\), so every encoding and arithmetic padding component must have expectation \(o(n^{-1})\); backward stability, an exact-dyadic assumption on Gaussian draws, or silent flush-to-zero behavior is insufficient.
body.honest_scope: The selected statistical kernel assumes known fixed rank, known homoskedastic Gaussian variance, square strong donor blocks, exact row and column span membership, and fixed incoherence and entry bounds. It does not claim unknown-rank adaptation, approximate-factor robustness, weak-donor inference, dependence robustness, or inference for a realized untreated outcome. In the regular rank-one special case it must reduce to the established Yan--Wainwright Gaussian formula. The observations remain continuously distributed Gaussian variables. The certified implementation applies a measurable finite-range dyadic encoding with an explicit exception flag, then invokes directed radix-two arithmetic on the encoded arrays; polynomial bit complexity, special-function enclosures, exceptional-state handling, negligible encoding transfer, and the rank-one joint-zero padding certificate remain explicitly open.
